To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of chlorinated polypropylenes (Cl-PP), and dimethyl glyoxine (DMC), to the polypropylene (pp) - thermotropic liquid crystallline copolyester (LCP) system, improves the interfacial interactions between the LCP phase and the matrix, and hence improves the mechanical and rheological properties of the system.
the thermal and visco-elastic properties of the ternary blend of PP, LCP and Cl-PP are improved in comparison with the corresponding binary blends.

(i) The interfacial interaction can be improved by the addition of chlorinated polypropylenes (Cl-PP); and (ii) The interfacional interaction can be further improved by the addition dimethylglyoxime (DMG) to ternary blend system containing PP-LCP-Cl-PP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermal and visco-elastic properties of polypropylene-thermotropic liquid crystalline copolymers blends.
the preparation, characterization, and processing of blends of polyolefins with thermotropic liquid crystal copolymers.
the effect of interfacial adhesion on the mechanical properties of PP-LCP blend systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal properties of the blends are determined by the degree of miscibility of the components, and the viscoelastic properties are governed by the interfacial interaction.
the addition of Cl-PP and DMG in ternary blend system of PP-LCP has a beneficial effect on the properties of PP-LCP blend system.
the addition of DMG to the PP-LCP system results in improved interfacial adhesion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of DMG and the presence of Cl-PP in ternary blends of PP and LCP improve interfacial interaction in the blend systems.
the addition of Cl-PP and DMG to the PP-LCP blend system is effective to improve the interfacial interaction.
blends of LCP with PP show a good balance of properties and are promising for commercial application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have been able to show that we can increase the interfacial adhesion of the LCP and PP by adding a compatibiliser to the PP-LCP blend.
the addition of a small amount of Cl-PP and DMG to a PP/LCP blend can improve the thermal and mechanical properties of the blend.
the use of a small amount of chlorinated polypropene (Cl-PP), as a compatibilizer, can be used to improve the interfacial interaction of the LCP and PP matrix.
